title: C482/963/2010 of SRI ARJUN NARAIN AND ANR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ANR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application (C-482) No. 963 of 2010
Arjun Narain and another ....... Applicants
 versus
State of Uttarakhand and another ....... Respondents
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, Advocate for the applicants.
Mr. Vipul Painuli, AGA for the State / respondent no. 1.
None present for respondent no. 2.
U.C. Dhyani, J. (oral)

The applicants, by means of present
application / petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., seek
to quash the charge-sheet dated 15.02.2010, submitted
against the applicants under Sections 420 and 120B of
IPC, as also cognizance order dated 23.04.2010, as well
as proceedings of criminal case no. 987 of 2010, State
vs Arjun Narain, arising out of case crime no. 519 of
2009, for the self-same offences, pending in the court of
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun.
2) An FIR was lodged by the informant
(respondent no. 2 herein) against accused-applicant no.
1 on 29.11.2009, at police station, Kotwali, Dehradun,
which was registered as case crime no. 519 of 2009,
under Section 420 of IPC. After the investigation, a
charge-sheet against applicant no. 1, as also applicant
no. 2 (wife of applicant no. 1), was submitted under
Sections 420 and 120B of IPC. Cognizance was taken

2
on the said charge-sheet and the accused persons were
summoned to face the trial for the said offences.
Aggrieved against the same, present application under
Section 482 of Cr.P.C. was filed on behalf of the
applicants.
3) As per FIR, applicant no. 1 borrowed a sum
of Rs. 3,80,000/- from respondent no. 2. When
applicant no. 1 did not return said money, respondent
no. 2 went to Kotwali, Dehradun in April 2009.
Respondent no. 2 went there to make a request to the
police to help him get repayment of the loan amount.
Kotwali police directed respondent no. 2 to go to police
station, Khurbura, before whom applicant no. 1 had
promised to repay the loan after four months. Instead
of returning the money, applicant no. 1 gave two
cheques of 1,90,000/- each to respondent no. 2.
Applicant no. 1 told respondent no. 2 that the payment
will be made in cash within two months and further told
him to take those cheques as security. Applicant no. 1
did not make payment in cash. Applicant no. 1 further
requested respondent no. 2 that he will soon arrange the
money and payment will be made to him. On
15.11.2009, at 11:00 A.M., applicant no. 1 took away
those cheques from respondent no. 2's wife, in his
absence. When respondent no. 2 contacted respondent
no. 2, he promised to give him other cheques in lieu of
those cheques, which he took away from his wife, in his
absence.

3
4) According to the informant, applicant no. 1
and his wife fixed up their meeting on 17.11.2009, at
07:00 P.M., in Anandam Sweets Shop. Respondent no.
2 reached Anandam Sweets Shop. Applicant no. 1 was
present there alongwith his wife. Applicant no. 1 told
respondent no. 2 to accompany him to police station,
Kotwali, where fresh cheques will be handed over to
him. Applicant no. 1 left his wife at Anandam Sweets
Shop and accompanied respondent no. 2 in his jeep.
Applicant no. 1 and respondent no. 2 reached Kotwali.
As soon as applicant no. 1 and respondent no. 2
proceeded from Anandam Sweets Shop, wife of
applicant no. 1 gave information to the police (at no.
100) that applicant no. 1 was kidnapped by respondent
no. 2, knowing it fully well that applicant no. 1 went
with respondent no. 2 in the vehicle on his own free
will. Applicants were, therefore, successful in
instituting a false case against respondent no. 2. The
said case was pending in the court. On 22.11.2009,
applicant no. 1 got a notice published in daily
newspaper 'Hindustan' regarding loss of his cheques.
In the said notice, it was mentioned that he had already
intimated Kotwali police on 28.10.2009, regarding loss
of those cheques. On 23.11.2009, it was revealed that
applicant no. 1 had already requested the bank on
18.11.2009 for 'stop payment'. Applicants have,
therefore, committed cheating. If applicant no. 1 had
intimated the police on 28.10.2009, then, why did he
not request the bank for 'stop payment' on that day?

4
Why the intimation was given 20 days later?
According to the informant (respondent no. 2 herein),
applicant no. 1 has misappropriated his money and he
was not interested in repaying the same to him.
5) Notice was issued to respondent no. 2.
Registry of this Court made an endorsement on
08.12.2010 that the notice was served personally upon
respondent no. 2. When the application under Section
482 of Cr.P.C. was listed again on 11.06.2013, this
Court directed the applicants to take fresh steps for
service of notice upon respondent no. 2. Steps were
again taken on the address given by respondent no. 2 in
the FIR. The postal packet containing notices was
returned with the endorsement that addressee did not
live at the given address. When the notice was once
served upon respondent no. 2 and he did not appear in
the Court, despite a lapse of about four years, therefore,
this Court proceeded to hear learned counsel for the
applicants and learned AGA for the respondent State.
6) Learned counsel for the applicants drew
attention of this Court towards Annexure no. 1, which
was a copy of FIR filed by applicant no. 2 against
respondent no. 2 and three others on 17.11.2009, at
police station, Kotwali, Dehradun, for the offences
punishable under Sections 323, 504, 363 of IPC. The
contention of learned counsel for the applicants is that
whereas applicant no. 2 lodged FIR against respondent

5
no. 2 and others on 17.11.2009, present FIR, which was
filed by respondent no. 2 against applicant no. 1 was
filed on 29.11.2009, and was a counterblast to the FIR
lodged by applicant no. 2 against respondent no. 2 and
others. In her FIR, applicant no. 2 alleged that on
17.11.2009, at 06:00 P.M., when her husband i.e.
applicant no. 1 was standing outside Anandam Sweets
Shop, respondent no. 2 came, threatened, abused,
caught hold and assaulted applicant no. 1. Husband of
applicant no. 2 was dragged inside a van and was
abducted by the accused persons. An information to
this effect was given to the police.
7) Learned counsel for the applicants further
contended that a criminal complaint case under Section
138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act was already
instituted by respondent no. 2 against applicant no. 1,
which is pending adjudication before Judicial
Magistrate (CBI), Dehradun (being criminal case no.
391 of 2010) and, therefore, proceedings against the
applicants should be quashed by this Court in exercise
of it's inherent jurisdiction.
8) A perusal of Annexure no. 6, which is a
copy of criminal complaint case no. 391 of 2010,
instituted by respondent no. 2 against applicant no. 1,
under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act
indicates that applicant no. 2 has already initiated
criminal proceedings for re-payment of Rs. 3,80,000/-

6
from applicant no. 1. Said criminal complaint case was
filed on 27.01.2010. Present FIR was filed by
respondent no. 2 against applicant no. 1 on 29.11.2009
in respect of the same amount i.e. 3,80,000/-. By way
of filing of said FIR, respondent no. 2 prayed for
repayment of said amount of Rs. 3,80,000/- to him by
applicant no. 1. Learned counsel for the applicants
stated that proceedings under Section 138 of the
Negotiable Instruments Act are already pending
adjudication for repayment of Rs. 3,80,000/-, which
relief was sought by respondent no. 2 by way of filing
FIR no. 519 of 2009. Simultaneous proceedings could
not be initiated or kept pending in relation to one relief
i.e. repayment of Rs. 3,80,000/-. FIR and the
proceedings arising out of FIR no. 519 of 2009 cannot
therefore be allowed to exist, primarily, in view of the
fact that a criminal case under Section 138 of the
Negotiable Insturments Act was pending between the
parties for the same relief.
9) There is yet another aspect of the matter. If
one looks at the FIR filed by applicant no. 2 against
respondent no. 2 and others and again looks at the
contents of present FIR, which was filed after a gap of
12 days, it appears that FIR no. 519 of 2009 was in the
form of explanation of FIR no. 507 of 2009, which was
filed under Sections 323, 504, 363 of IPC. FIR no. 519
of 2009 was lodged as a matter of giving explanation to
the offence under Section 363 of IPC., i.e., the

7
circumstances under which applicant no. 1
accompanied respondent no. 2 in his jeep to Kotwali,
Dehradun. FIR no. 509 of 2009, therefore, smacks of
abuse of the process of the Court.
10) Hon'ble Apex Court in Amit Kapoor vs
Ramesh Chander and another, (2013) 1 SCC (Cri) 986,
had held that where the exercise of power under Section
482 of Cr.P.C. is essential to prevent patent miscarriage
of justice and for correcting some grave error that may
be committed by the subordinate court, such power
should be exercised by the High Courts ex debito
justitiae, i.e., to do real and substantial justice for
administration of which alone, the courts exist.
11) Although inherent powers of this Court
under Section 482 Cr.P.C. should be exercised
sparingly, carefully and with caution and only when
such exercise is justified by the tests specifically laid
down in the Section itself but the instant case appears to
be one such case in which such jurisdiction should be
exercised.
12) This Court, therefore, is of the opinion that
summoning of the accused-applicants, in the particular
circumstances of the present criminal case, should be
set aside to prevent abuse of the process of the Court.

8
13) Application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is,
accordingly, allowed. Charge-sheet dated 15.02.2010,
submitted against the applicants under Sections 420 and
120B of IPC, as also cognizance order dated
23.04.2010, as well as proceedings of criminal case no.
987 of 2010, State vs Arjun Narain, arising out of case
crime no. 519 of 2009, for the self-same offences,
pending in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Dehradun are hereby quashed qua applicants.
